I am preparing for a faculty meeting where we need to review quiz performance across our Fall 2014 courses. I need you to pull quiz data from our learning management system for all courses offered in that semester and summarize the results.

Scope definition (important, follow exactly): our LMS hosts the same subjects across multiple semesters (Fall 2013, Spring 2013, Spring 2014, Fall 2014), and the semester is identified by the suffix in the course name. "Fall 2014 courses" means exactly the courses whose Canvas course name ends with "(Fall 2014)": Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014), Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014), Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014), Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014), Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014), Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014), and Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014). Do not include any course whose name ends with a different semester suffix, and do not select courses by date ranges or enrollment terms — match on the course-name suffix only. Among these seven courses, only the ones that actually have quizzes in the LMS should appear in the outputs (a course with no quizzes at all is omitted entirely).

For each of those Fall 2014 courses, gather the quiz titles, the number of student submissions per quiz, the average score, the minimum score, and the maximum score. Count every quiz submission recorded in Canvas for that quiz regardless of its submission date, and compute the average/minimum/maximum over the submission scores. Then create an Excel spreadsheet called Quiz_Performance.xlsx in the workspace. The spreadsheet should have a sheet named "Quiz Details" with columns Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, and Max_Score. The Course column must contain the full Canvas course name including the "(Fall 2014)" suffix, e.g. "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)". The Avg_Score, Min_Score, and Max_Score should be rounded to two decimal places. Sort the rows first by Course name alphabetically, then by Quiz_Title alphabetically within each course.

Also add a second sheet called "Course Summary" that aggregates at the course level over the same quiz-bearing Fall 2014 courses. It should have columns Course (again the full course name with the "(Fall 2014)" suffix), Total_Quizzes (number of quizzes in that course), Total_Submissions (sum across all quizzes), and Overall_Avg_Score which is the weighted average of quiz scores across all submissions for that course rounded to two decimal places, i.e. sum(avg_score * submissions) / sum(submissions) over the course's quizzes. Sort alphabetically by Course.

Finally, create a PowerPoint presentation called Quiz_Report.pptx in the workspace. The first slide should be a title slide with the title "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report" and subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary". Then create one dedicated slide per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course with the course name as the title and a text body listing the number of quizzes, total submissions, and overall average score for that course. Add a final slide with the title "Key Takeaways" and body text stating which course had the highest overall average score and which had the lowest.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the large quiz-submission reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave, freeze the gathered statistics into a single JSON handoff file, and let the main agent itself build both deliverables — no planning sub-agent, no second wave.

The main agent first resolves the runtime workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the seven fixed Fall 2014 courses by full-name suffix "(Fall 2014)" (never by date range or enrollment term). Then, natively in parallel, it calls canvas_list_quizzes once per retained course and records each course's literal quiz_ids. A course with zero quizzes is omitted from all outputs. Before dispatch, freeze one assignment manifest entry per quiz-bearing course: course_id|course_name|quiz_ids.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course below. Omit zero-quiz courses from this wave.

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)": fetch the full quiz-submission records for every quiz in its course (canvas quiz-submission listing, per_page=100, follow pagination.has_page/pagination.has_more, and always read the FULL JSON from the output_path file when the chat preview is truncated); count every recorded submission regardless of date; compute per quiz Submissions (count), Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score over the submission scores; aggregate at course level Total_Quizzes, Total_Submissions, and Overall_Avg_Score = sum(avg_score * submissions) / sum(submissions); and return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id, course_name, quizzes: [{quiz_title, submissions, avg_score, min_score, max_score}], total_quizzes, total_submissions, overall_avg_score}. Strictly read-only with respect to Canvas; do not write workspace files, do not return the raw row set.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" — same literal recipe, only its assignment string substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" — same literal recipe, only its assignment string substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies every handoff in one single pass (exactly one per manifest entry, non-null statistics, submission counts > 0), then freezes ALL rows into workspace/quiz_data.json — the single handoff for the outputs — and builds both deliverables itself with no further delegation: (a) Quiz_Performance.xlsx with sheet "Quiz Details" (Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score; full course names including the "(Fall 2014)" suffix; scores rounded to two decimals; sorted by Course then Quiz_Title) and sheet "Course Summary" (Course, Total_Quizzes, Total_Submissions, Overall_Avg_Score; sorted by Course), reading both populated ranges back; (b) Quiz_Report.pptx with a title slide "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report" / subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary", one slide per quiz-bearing course titled with the full course name and listing its quiz count, total submissions and overall average score, and a final "Key Takeaways" slide naming the courses with the highest and lowest overall average scores, verified through presentation info and text extraction. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back and the deck, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

You are helping me gather quiz submission statistics from a Canvas LMS for a faculty meeting report.

Your specific task: For course ID 7 (Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)), use the Canvas MCP tools to fetch ALL assignment submissions for these 4 assignments:
- assignment_id 65 (quiz "CMA 24295")
- assignment_id 66 (quiz "CMA 24296")
- assignment_id 67 (quiz "CMA 24297")
- assignment_id 68 (quiz "CMA 24298")

Use the tool `mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignment_submissions` with `per_page=100` and iterate through ALL pages (use `page=1`, `page=2`, etc., until `pagination.has_more` is false). The summary in each response includes `total_count` so you know how many pages there are.

For each assignment, extract ALL submission scores (the `score` field). Then compute:
- Number of submissions (n)
- Average score (mean of all scores)
- Minimum score
- Maximum score

Important: Each submission record has a `score` field (e.g. "56.00"). Treat all of them as numbers. Don't worry about duplicates — count each submission once.

Return your final result as plain text in this exact format for each assignment:

ASSIGNMENT <assignment_id> (<quiz title>):
  submissions=<n>
  avg=<rounded to 2 decimals>
  min=<rounded to 2 decimals>
  max=<rounded to 2 decimals>

You may need to make up to 20 page calls per assignment (1917 / 100 ≈ 20 pages). Make all page calls for one assignment before moving to the next, but you can interleave calls across assignments if you want to be more efficient. The page counts for the 4 assignments in this course are similar (~20 pages each).

Use the workspace's Python execute tool (`mcp__local__python_execute`) to save intermediate JSON outputs to files if helpful — the .tool_results directory under /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_MiniMax-M3/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-analysis-ppt/workspace/.tool_results can hold them.

At the end, output a clear summary with the 4 lines in the format above. Do NOT create the Excel or PowerPoint files — that's my job.
Fetch assignment submissions for course 7
